title: U.S. House · South Carolina's 3rd District

candidates.name: Sheri Biggs
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced without a primary after the Republican primary was canceled

summary.text: Sheri Biggs is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for South Carolina's 3rd District, elected in 2024 to her first term of public office and seeking re-election. A nurse practitioner and Air National Guard officer, she describes a career of more than three decades in health care before entering Congress. According to her campaign website, she is running on a platform she calls "Healing our Nation" as a pro-life, pro-Second Amendment Republican.

background.text: Born in Mississippi in 1970.

Earned a Doctor of Nursing Practice from Samford University. Her official House biography says her bachelor's degree, from Carolina Bible College, is in Christian Ministries, and that she has completed advanced coursework at Air War College.

Serves as a Lieutenant Colonel in the Air National Guard. Her official biography says she received the Aerial Achievement Medal and served as a medical crew director on combat and combat-support missions in support of Operation Freedom's Sentinel.

According to her official biography, she has worked more than three decades in health care, as an Intensive Care Unit nurse, a licensed nursing home administrator and a health services consultant, and is a board-certified family nurse practitioner and psychiatric mental health nurse practitioner.

Volunteers with veterans' and first responders' mental health needs, and, according to her official biography, with the Dream Center and other community and veterans organizations; she is a member of Temple Baptist Church in Anderson, where she provides counseling.

Won the 2024 Republican primary runoff for South Carolina's 3rd District over Mark Burns, then won the November 2024 general election over Democrat Bryon Best and Michael Bedenbaugh. The seat was previously held by Jeff Duncan.
Took office in January 2025. Her official biography describes her as the third woman from South Carolina elected to the U.S. House and the first to represent the 3rd District.
Serves on the House Homeland Security, Foreign Affairs, and Science, Space, and Technology Committees.
Her campaign website describes her as a wife and mother who lives in Salem, South Carolina.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Homeland Security (Border Security and Enforcement; Transportation and Maritime Security subcommittees), the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology (Energy; Research and Technology subcommittees), and the Committee on Foreign Affairs (2025-2026 assignments).

candidates.name: Eunice Lehmacher
candidates.ballotNote: Won the Democratic primary (June 9, 2026) with 53.4% of the vote

summary.text: Eunice Lehmacher is a retired medical social worker and psychotherapist from Clemson and the Democratic nominee for South Carolina's 3rd District. She has worked as a counselor, teacher, librarian and church educator, serves on two local bodies, and previously ran unsuccessfully for the South Carolina House in 2020 and 2024. According to her Ballotpedia survey, her campaign emphasizes health care access, energy costs and affordability.

background.text: Born in Lexington, Missouri, and grew up in Wilson, North Carolina, and Knoxville, Tennessee.

Earned a high school diploma from South Young High School, a bachelor's degree from Concordia University (1985), and a master's degree from the Catholic University of America in Washington, D.C. (1996).
Her career includes work as a high school math and science teacher, library associate and church educator, according to Ballotpedia.
Moved to Clemson, South Carolina, with her husband in 2002, where they raised two sons, according to her Ballotpedia survey.

Worked as a medical social worker and psychotherapist for Oconee Memorial Hospital, Clemson University, Hospice of the Foothills and other health care agencies, and owned a private counseling practice in Seneca, SC.
Was the Democratic nominee for South Carolina House of Representatives District 3 in 2020 and 2024, losing the general election to Jerry Carter (R) in 2020 and to Phillip Bowers (R) in 2024.
Serves by gubernatorial appointment on the Anderson Oconee Pickens Mental Health Commission and on the Sustainability Advisory Committee for the City of Clemson.

Describes volunteer work teaching classes, leading support groups, mentoring students and leading community groups including the Sierra Club and her neighborhood association; has been affiliated with the South Carolina Society for Clinical Social Workers and the Clinical Social Work Association.
Won the June 9, 2026 Democratic primary with 53.4 percent of the vote over Ernest Mackins.

priorities.text: Increasing access to healthcare, especially in rural areas: restoring funding for Medicaid and the ACA, lowering the Medicare eligibility age to 64, and increasing funding for NIH/NIMH health research.
priorities.quote: I want to restore funding for Medicaid and the ACA and increase access to Medicare (e.g. lower the eligibility age to 64).

priorities.text: Helping residents with high prices, including opposing funding for ICE and long-term detention of legal immigrants and increasing apprenticeship and job-training opportunities.

candidates.name: Brian Corriea
candidates.ballotNote: Nominated at the Libertarian Party convention on April 11, 2026

summary.text: Brian Corriea is the Libertarian Party nominee for South Carolina's 3rd District. According to his campaign website, he is a Navy veteran, husband and father from Williamston, SC, running a self-funded campaign that accepts no donations.

background.text: According to his campaign website, he served nine years in the U.S. Navy.
Describes himself as a libertarian and as a husband and father who lives in Williamston, South Carolina.
Advanced from the Libertarian Party convention on April 11, 2026; his campaign website says the campaign is entirely self-funded and refuses all donations.
